# Welcome

> This site is not ready for public consumption. Rough outlines are being created, many times with the help of AI. I'm building this in public and will continuously refine and fill in the gaps.

- [Welcome](https://wshaddix.com/index.md): Welcome

## Getting Started

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/getting-started/overview.md): Welcome! This site is a comprehensive guide to software engineering - from fundamentals to leadership.
- [Prerequisites](https://wshaddix.com/getting-started/prerequisites.md): What you should know before diving into this material.
- [Workstation Setup](https://wshaddix.com/getting-started/workstation-setup.md): You are going to be looking at your desktop a lot, so pick a background that brings you happiness. Every time you look at it you should feel joy and excitement.
- [Learning Path](https://wshaddix.com/getting-started/learning-path.md): A roadmap through the material based on your experience level. Most pages are outlines. Each one will grow a C# sample, with a companion .cs file when the sample is longer than about 30 lines.

## AI-Assisted Development

- [AI-Assisted Development](https://wshaddix.com/ai-assisted-development/overview.md): How to use an assistant while you design, write, and review software. The assistant is a tool in the loop. You still own the change.
- [Terms](https://wshaddix.com/ai-assisted-development/terms.md): A short glossary. Later pages use these words without redefining them.
- [Tools](https://wshaddix.com/ai-assisted-development/tools.md): The categories of assistant you will meet. Product names change. The categories do not.
- [Techniques](https://wshaddix.com/ai-assisted-development/techniques.md): Ways of working that make an assistant useful on a real change.
- [Prompting](https://wshaddix.com/ai-assisted-development/prompting.md): A prompt is a specification for one turn. It has a goal, constraints, and the context the model would otherwise invent.
- [Context and Instructions](https://wshaddix.com/ai-assisted-development/context-and-instructions.md): The model only knows what is in the window. You decide what that is.
- [Verification](https://wshaddix.com/ai-assisted-development/verification.md): Generated code is a draft. The same checks apply as if a new teammate wrote it.
- [Using MCP](https://wshaddix.com/ai-assisted-development/using-mcp.md): MCP lets an assistant call a tool on a server: read a ticket, query a database, or hit an API. Building the server is covered under C#.
- [Risks and Limits](https://wshaddix.com/ai-assisted-development/risks-and-limits.md): The failure modes that show up in a team that uses assistants every day.

## Fundamentals

### Data Structures

- [Trees & Graphs](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/data-structures/trees-graphs.md): Trees and graphs represent hierarchical and networked relationships between data.
- [Hash Tables](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/data-structures/hash-tables.md): A hash table (hash map, dictionary) stores key-value pairs with average O(1) lookup, insert, and delete operations.
- [Stacks & Queues](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/data-structures/stacks-queues.md): Stacks and queues are abstract data types (ADTs) that restrict how elements are added and removed, providing specific ordering guarantees.
- [Linked Lists](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/data-structures/linked-lists.md): A linked list is a sequence of nodes where each node contains data and a reference (pointer) to the next node.
- [Arrays](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/data-structures/arrays.md): Arrays are the most fundamental data structure - a contiguous block of memory storing elements of the same type.

### Algorithms

- [Recursion](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/algorithms/recursion.md): Recursion is a technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller instance of the same problem.
- [Searching Algorithms](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/algorithms/searching.md): Searching is finding an element in a data structure. The right algorithm depends on the structure and whether data is sorted.
- [Sorting Algorithms](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/algorithms/sorting.md): Sorting is arranging items in a specific order. Understanding sorting algorithms teaches you algorithmic thinking and complexity trade-offs.
- [Big O Notation](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/algorithms/big-o-notation.md): Big O notation describes how an algorithm's time or space requirements grow as input size increases. It's the language engineers use to discuss performance.

### Programming Concepts

- [OOP Principles](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/programming-concepts/oop-principles.md): Object-oriented programming (OOP) organizes code around objects that contain data and behavior. These principles help you write maintainable, flexible code.
- [Functional Concepts](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/programming-concepts/functional-concepts.md): Functional programming (FP) treats computation as the evaluation of mathematical functions, emphasizing immutability and avoiding side effects.
- [Concurrency](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/programming-concepts/concurrency.md): Concurrency is managing multiple tasks that can be in progress at the same time. Parallelism is actually executing multiple tasks simultaneously.
- [Error Handling](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/programming-concepts/error-handling.md): How a program reports failure, and what the caller is owed.
- [Memory and Garbage Collection](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/programming-concepts/memory-and-gc.md): Where values live while a C# program runs, and who frees them.

### Networking

- [HTTP and the Web](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/networking/http.md): How a request moves from a browser or an HttpClient to a server and back. Read this before building an API.

### Security

- [Security Concepts](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/security/overview.md): The failures a feature developer meets, before any framework. The C# pages show how ASP.NET Core implements the controls.
- [Authentication and Authorization](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/security/authentication-and-authorization.md): Authentication answers who the caller is. Authorization answers what that caller may do. The two checks fail in different ways.

### Distributed Systems

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/distributed-systems/overview.md): Work that spans more than one process, and the guarantees you give up when it does.
- [Consistency](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/distributed-systems/consistency.md): Each operation picks how up to date the data has to be.
- [Failure and Degradation](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/distributed-systems/failure-and-degradation.md): Plan for the failure you did not write a test for.
- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/fundamentals/overview.md): This section covers the foundational computer science concepts that every software engineer should understand. These concepts transcend any specific programming language and form the bedrock of software engineering expertise.

## C#

### Language Basics

- [Getting Started](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/language-basics/getting-started.md): This guide will get you writing C# code quickly.
- [Projects and Solutions](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/language-basics/projects-and-solutions.md): A solution is a set of projects. A project compiles to an assembly. This is the unit you build, reference, and ship.
- [Types and Variables](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/language-basics/types.md): C# is a strongly-typed language. Understanding its type system is fundamental.
- [Control Flow](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/language-basics/control-flow.md): Controlling the execution path through your code.
- [Methods and Parameters](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/language-basics/methods.md): Methods are the building blocks of behavior in C#.
- [Classes and Objects](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/language-basics/classes.md): Object-oriented programming in C#.
- [Nullability](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/language-basics/nullability.md): Nullable reference types make a missing value visible at compile time.
- [Exceptions](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/language-basics/exceptions.md): How C# reports a failure that the current method cannot finish.
- [Collections](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/language-basics/collections.md): Storing and organizing groups of objects.
- [Delegates and Lambdas](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/language-basics/delegates-and-lambdas.md): A delegate is a method you can pass around. Lambdas and events are built on that.
- [Disposal](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/language-basics/disposal.md): The garbage collector frees memory. It does not close files, sockets, or database connections.
- [Files, Streams, and JSON](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/language-basics/files-streams-and-json.md): Reading and writing bytes, text, and JSON.
- [Dates and Culture](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/language-basics/dates-and-culture.md): Instants, local times, and text that depends on a culture.

### Advanced Features

- [Generics](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/advanced-features/generics.md): Write type-safe, reusable code without sacrificing performance.
- [LINQ](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/advanced-features/linq.md): Query collections with a consistent, expressive syntax.
- [Async/Await](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/advanced-features/async.md): Write asynchronous code that reads like synchronous code.
- [Cancellation](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/advanced-features/cancellation.md): Cooperative cancellation, and a limit on how much work runs at once.
- [Records](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/advanced-features/records.md): Immutable data types with value semantics.
- [Pattern Matching](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/advanced-features/pattern-matching.md): Declarative way to check and destructure data.
- [High-Performance C#](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/advanced-features/high-performance-csharp.md): Primitives you reach for when an ordinary allocation shows up on a hot path.
- [Attributes](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/advanced-features/attributes.md): Attributes attach metadata to code. Validation, JSON, and MCP tools all read that metadata.
- [Modern C#](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/advanced-features/modern-csharp.md): Language features you will see in current .NET code. Each one is small. Together they are the dialect this site uses.

### Platform

- [The .NET Platform](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/platform/overview.md): Console apps, MCP servers, APIs, Blazor, WinUI, and Uno are composed the same way: a host, a service container, configuration, and logging.
- [Generic Host](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/platform/generic-host.md): The host builds configuration, the service provider, and logging, then runs until it is stopped.
- [.NET Aspire](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/platform/aspire.md): Orchestrate the local dependencies of a multi-project app.
- [Dependency Injection](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/platform/dependency-injection.md): A type asks for what it needs. The container creates it.
- [Configuration and Options](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/platform/configuration-and-options.md): Settings come from files, environment variables, and user secrets. Code reads them through the options pattern.
- [Logging](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/platform/logging.md): ILogger is the logging abstraction. The sink (console, file, or a vendor) is a registration.
- [HTTP Clients](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/platform/http-clients.md): One way to call HTTP from a console app, an API, Blazor, WinUI, Uno, and an MCP server.
- [Publishing](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/platform/publishing.md): How a project becomes a program you can run on another machine.

### Console Apps

- [Console Apps](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/console/overview.md): A console app is the smallest host: configuration, logging, and a job that exits with a code.
- [Command-Line Parsing](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/console/command-line.md): Parse arguments with System.CommandLine so a tool has help text, subcommands, and typed options.

### Entity Framework

- [Getting Started](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/entity-framework/getting-started.md): Entity Framework Core is Microsoft's recommended ORM for .NET applications.
- [DbContext](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/entity-framework/dbcontext.md): The central class for database interaction in EF Core.
- [Modeling](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/entity-framework/modeling.md): How a C# model becomes tables. Conventions first, then Fluent API where a convention is wrong.
- [Querying](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/entity-framework/querying.md): Using LINQ to query databases.
- [Change Tracking](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/entity-framework/change-tracking.md): A context remembers the entities it loaded. That memory is how SaveChanges knows what to write.
- [Migrations](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/entity-framework/migrations.md): Evolving your database schema over time.
- [Transactions](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/entity-framework/transactions.md): SaveChanges is already one transaction. You open your own when more than one save must commit together.
- [Concurrency](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/entity-framework/concurrency.md): How two saves of the same row avoid a lost update.
- [Performance](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/entity-framework/performance.md): Avoiding common performance pitfalls.
- [Seeding](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/entity-framework/seeding.md): Reference data the app assumes is present.
- [Raw SQL](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/entity-framework/raw-sql.md): LINQ is the default. SQL is for a query LINQ cannot express, or a procedure the database already owns.
- [Testing Entity Framework](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/entity-framework/testing.md): Test against a relational database. The in-memory provider does not enforce the constraints your production database enforces.

### ASP.NET Core

#### Web APIs

- [Web APIs](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/overview.md): HTTP APIs on ASP.NET Core. Each child page is an outline that will grow a C# sample.
- [APIs for Agents](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/apis-for-agents.md): An HTTP API whose caller is a model choosing a tool.
- [Idempotent Requests](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/idempotent-requests.md): A client that retries a POST needs the server to recognize the same attempt.
- [Minimal APIs and Controllers](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/minimal-apis-and-controllers.md): ASP.NET Core has two ways to declare an endpoint. Pick one per project and stay with it unless a feature forces the other.
- [Routing and Model Binding](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/routing-and-binding.md): How a request URL and body become arguments on a handler.
- [Validation](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/validation.md): Reject a request that cannot succeed before any state changes.
- [Error Handling](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/error-handling.md): One error shape for the whole API, so every client parses failures the same way.
- [OpenAPI](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/openapi.md): OpenAPI is the contract. Swagger UI is one way to read it.
- [CORS](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/cors.md): Browsers refuse a cross-origin call unless the API says it is allowed. Non-browser clients ignore CORS.
- [Rate Limiting](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/rate-limiting.md): The built-in rate limiter slows a caller down before they crowd out everyone else.
- [Pagination, Filtering, and Sorting](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/pagination.md): List endpoints return a page, not a table.
- [Background Services](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/background-services.md): Work that must finish even though the HTTP request already returned.
- [gRPC](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/grpc.md): A contract-first RPC API that runs on HTTP/2.
- [SignalR](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/signalr.md): A persistent connection so the server can push a message to a Blazor, WinUI, or Uno client.
- [Polling, Server-Sent Events, and Async Request-Reply](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/polling-sse-and-async-request-reply.md): Ways to deliver a result after the first request has returned.
- [API Versioning](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/versioning.md): How a contract changes without breaking a client you already shipped.
- [Caching](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/web-apis/caching.md): Cache a response when the bytes do not depend on a side effect.

#### Authentication

- [Authentication](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/authentication/overview.md): How an ASP.NET Core app establishes who the caller is. Pick the scheme on the choosing page before implementing any of the others.
- [Choosing a Scheme](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/authentication/choosing-a-scheme.md): The caller decides the scheme. A browser, a service, a Windows app, and a phone do not hold credentials the same way.
- [ASP.NET Core Identity](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/authentication/identity.md): Identity stores users, passwords, and roles. It is the user database, not the wire protocol.
- [Cookie Authentication](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/authentication/cookies.md): Cookie authentication is the session for a browser app, including Blazor.
- [JWT Bearer](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/authentication/jwt.md): A JSON Web Token is a signed set of claims. The API checks the signature, the issuer, the audience, and the expiry.
- [Refresh Tokens](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/authentication/refresh-tokens.md): An access token is short-lived. A refresh token gets the next one without asking for the password again.
- [OpenID Connect](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/authentication/openid-connect.md): OpenID Connect is how WinUI, Uno, and a web app sign in with an external provider such as Microsoft Entra ID.
- [Modern Authentication](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/authentication/modern-auth.md): Schemes that sit next to passwords, cookies, and bearer tokens.

#### Authorization

- [Authorization](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/authorization/overview.md): Authorization runs after authentication. A valid token is not permission to do the thing.
- [Permission-Based Authorization](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/authorization/permissions.md): A permission names one action the caller may perform.
- [Resource-Based Authorization](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/authorization/resource-based.md): The question is not only whether the caller is an editor. It is whether they may edit this row.

#### Middleware

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/middleware/overview.md): Components that handle requests and responses in a pipeline.

#### Hosting

- [Kestrel and HTTPS](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/hosting/kestrel-and-https.md): Kestrel is the server. In production it usually sits behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS.

#### Observability

- [Observability](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/observability/overview.md): Logs, metrics, and traces from the running API. Alerting and the operational response live in the DevOps monitoring pages.
- [Health Checks](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/observability/health-checks.md): A health endpoint tells a platform whether to send traffic.

#### Blazor

- [Blazor](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/blazor/overview.md): Blazor is the C# web UI. It talks to the API. It does not become a second place where business rules live.
- [AI Features](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/blazor/ai-features.md): A Blazor component that shows a model's answer. The prompt and the model key stay on the server.
- [Components and Routing](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/blazor/components-and-routing.md): A component is a .razor file with parameters, and the router picks one from the URL.
- [Forms and Validation](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/blazor/forms-and-validation.md): A form edits a model and shows the same kind of field errors the API returns.
- [Blazor Authentication](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/blazor/authentication.md): A Blazor app in the browser uses the cookie scheme. It does not store a JWT where script can read it.
- [Calling the API from Blazor](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/blazor/calling-the-api.md): Components call a typed client. They do not build URLs by hand.
- [JavaScript Interop](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/aspnet-core/blazor/javascript-interop.md): Call a browser API when C# cannot. Keep the boundary small.

### Clients

- [Clients](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/clients/overview.md): WinUI and Uno share this layer. Blazor borrows the HTTP and auth parts and keeps its own UI model.
- [MVVM](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/clients/mvvm.md): A view binds to a view model. The view model calls a service. CommunityToolkit.Mvvm generates the boilerplate.
- [XAML](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/clients/xaml.md): WinUI and Uno share the WinUI XAML dialect. Differences belong on the Uno page, not in a second copy of this one.
- [HTTP and Auth](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/clients/http-and-auth.md): A WinUI or Uno client calls the API with a typed client and attaches a bearer token.
- [Navigation and Storage](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/clients/navigation-and-storage.md): How a client moves between pages, and where it keeps settings and tokens.
- [Accessibility](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/clients/accessibility.md): A control has a name a screen reader can say, and a way to reach it without a pointer.

### WinUI 3

- [WinUI 3](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/winui/overview.md): WinUI 3 is the native Windows UI on the Windows App SDK. It uses the shared XAML and MVVM pages.
- [Lifecycle and Windowing](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/winui/lifecycle-and-windowing.md): A WinUI app has a window, and the process can be suspended only in the packaged model.
- [Packaging](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/winui/packaging.md): A packaged app is an MSIX. An unpackaged app is an executable you copy. They differ in identity, updates, and which APIs work.
- [WinUI Authentication](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/winui/authentication.md): The protocol is the same OpenID Connect flow as Uno. Windows can broker the account through the system.

### Uno Platform

- [Uno Platform](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/uno/overview.md): Uno runs a WinUI-style XAML app on iOS, Android, WebAssembly, and desktop. The shared code is the WinUI code. The platform page is for the differences.
- [Uno Project Structure](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/uno/project-structure.md): An Uno solution has one shared project and a head per platform.
- [Platform-Specific Code](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/uno/platform-specific-code.md): Most of the app is shared. A camera, a file picker, or a secure store is not.
- [Uno Authentication](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/uno/authentication.md): The protocol is OpenID Connect with PKCE. This page is the mobile and WebAssembly client.
- [Publishing Uno Apps](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/uno/publishing.md): Each target has its own package and its own store rules.

### MCP Servers

- [MCP Servers](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/mcp/overview.md): A Model Context Protocol server exposes tools, resources, and prompts to an AI client. In C# it is a hosted process, either on standard I/O or on HTTP.
- [MCP Clients and Agents](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/mcp/clients-and-agents.md): An MCP client calls a server. An agent uses that client when a model asks for a tool.
- [Tools, Resources, and Prompts](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/mcp/tools-resources-and-prompts.md): Tools do something. Resources are data the model can read. Prompts are reusable instructions.
- [Hosting an MCP Server](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/mcp/hosting.md): The same server can run as a local stdio process or as an HTTP endpoint.
- [MCP Authentication](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/mcp/authentication.md): A local stdio server runs as the user. A remote HTTP server has to know who is calling.

### Security

- [Security](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/security/overview.md): Platform controls that sit under every app type. The concepts are in Fundamentals. Authentication and authorization have their own ASP.NET Core sections.
- [Secrets](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/security/secrets.md): A secret in a repository is a published secret.
- [Sensitive Data in Logs](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/security/sensitive-data-in-logs.md): A value written to a log is copied into every sink that stores that log.
- [Transport and Headers](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/security/transport-and-headers.md): TLS is the floor. Response headers close a set of browser mistakes.
- [Data Protection](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/security/data-protection.md): ASP.NET Core encrypts cookies and tokens with a key ring. More than one server means a shared ring.

### Testing

- [TUnit Project Setup](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/testing/project-setup.md): Tests on this site run on TUnit. A test project is an executable that discovers tests at compile time. It is not an xUnit, NUnit, or MSTest project.
- [Unit Testing](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/testing/unit-testing.md): A unit test checks one behavior of one type. Collaborators are replaced so the test does not touch a database, the network, or the clock. The runner is TUnit.
- [Mocking](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/testing/mocking.md): A mock stands in for a collaborator so the test can decide what that collaborator returns and can check that it was called. This site uses TUnit.Mocks.
- [Time-Dependent Code](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/testing/time-dependent-code.md): Tests that depend on the clock should take a clock you control.
- [Integration Testing](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/testing/integration-testing.md): An integration test checks that two or more real parts work together. On this site that usually means the API, the database, or both. The runner is still TUnit.
- [ASP.NET Core Tests](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/testing/webapplicationfactory.md): API tests boot the app in-process with TUnit.AspNetCore. Use TestWebApplicationFactoryTEntryPoint, not the vanilla WebApplicationFactoryT, so traces and logs stay tied to the test that made the call.
- [Testcontainers](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/testing/testcontainers.md): A test can start a real SQL Server in Docker and throw it away when the test session ends.
- [bUnit](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/testing/bunit.md): bUnit renders a Blazor component in memory. It runs on TUnit the same way any other test does.

#### Reqnroll

- [Reqnroll](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/testing/reqnroll/overview.md): Reqnroll turns a Gherkin feature file into a test. On this site the test runner is TUnit, through the Reqnroll.TUnit package. Reqnroll supports TUnit 1.3.25 and later, on .NET 8 and later.
- [Feature Files](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/testing/reqnroll/feature-files.md): A feature file is the spec. The sentence is the contract. The binding is an implementation detail.
- [Step Definitions](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/testing/reqnroll/step-definitions.md): A step definition is a method whose attribute matches a sentence in the feature file.
- [Hooks and Context](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/testing/reqnroll/hooks-and-context.md): Hooks set up a scenario. Context injection passes that setup into the steps.
- [Living Documentation](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/testing/reqnroll/living-documentation.md): A feature file that no longer matches the product is a false document. The test run is what keeps it honest.
- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/csharp/overview.md): C# is a modern, object-oriented programming language developed by Microsoft. Combined with the .NET platform, it's one of the most versatile ecosystems for building applications.

## Databases

### Relational

- [SQL Fundamentals](https://wshaddix.com/databases/relational/sql-fundamentals.md): Structured Query Language (SQL) is the standard language for relational databases.
- [Database Design](https://wshaddix.com/databases/relational/database-design.md): Designing databases that are efficient, maintainable, and correct.
- [Indexes and Query Plans](https://wshaddix.com/databases/relational/indexes-and-query-plans.md): Why a query is fast or slow, and how an index changes the plan.
- [Transactions and Isolation](https://wshaddix.com/databases/relational/transactions-and-isolation.md): How a group of writes becomes one atomic change, and the anomalies each isolation level allows.

#### SQL Server

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/databases/relational/sql-server/overview.md): Microsoft's enterprise relational database system.

### NoSQL

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/databases/nosql/overview.md): Non-relational databases optimized for specific data models and access patterns.
- [Redis and Caching](https://wshaddix.com/databases/nosql/redis.md): A cache and a short-lived store next to SQL Server. SQL remains the system of record.

### Data Modeling

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/databases/data-modeling/overview.md): Designing data structures that serve your application effectively.
- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/databases/overview.md): Databases are the backbone of most applications. Understanding how to design, query, and optimize databases is essential for any software engineer.

## Patterns

### Coding Patterns (GoF)

#### Creational Patterns

- [Abstract factory pattern](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/coding-patterns/creational-patterns/abstract-factory-pattern.md)
- [Builder pattern](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/coding-patterns/creational-patterns/builder-pattern.md)
- [Factory method pattern](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/coding-patterns/creational-patterns/factory-method-pattern.md)
- [Prototype pattern](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/coding-patterns/creational-patterns/prototype-pattern.md)
- [Singleton pattern](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/coding-patterns/creational-patterns/singleton-pattern.md)

#### Structural Patterns

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/coding-patterns/structural-patterns/overview.md): Structural patterns deal with object composition - how classes and objects are combined to form larger structures.
- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/coding-patterns/overview.md): The "Gang of Four" design patterns, from the book Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software by Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, and John Vlissides, are 23 classic software design patterns.

#### Behavioral Patterns

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/coding-patterns/behavioral-patterns/overview.md): Behavioral patterns are concerned with algorithms and the assignment of responsibilities between objects.
- [Decorator](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/coding-patterns/decorator.md): A decorator wraps an object and adds behavior without changing the object's type. Middleware and HTTP handlers are decorators.

### Architecture Styles

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/architecture-styles/overview.md): How a codebase is sliced, and how those slices are kept from leaking.
- [Modular Monolith](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/architecture-styles/modular-monolith.md): One deployable, divided into modules that own their data and their features.
- [Architecture Tests](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/architecture-styles/architecture-tests.md): Tests that fail when code reaches across a boundary you meant to keep.
- [Event Sourcing and Change Data Capture](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/architecture-styles/event-sourcing-and-cdc.md): Two ways a change becomes a stream of facts.

### Application Patterns

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/application-patterns/overview.md): This page is a catalog of names, not a lesson. The patterns this path teaches are Repository and CQRS.
- [Repository](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/application-patterns/repository.md): A repository is a collection-shaped front for one aggregate. DbContext is already a unit of work, so a second unit-of-work wrapper needs a reason.
- [CQRS](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/application-patterns/cqrs.md): Separate the model that changes state from the model that reads it, when those two models want different shapes.

### Integration Patterns

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/integration-patterns/overview.md): This page is a catalog of names, not a lesson. Messaging shows up in practice in background services and in Building a SaaS: Background Jobs.
- [Outbox and the Idempotent Consumer](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/integration-patterns/outbox-and-idempotent-consumer.md): Saving state and sending a message are two writes, and either one can fail on its own.
- [Sagas](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/integration-patterns/sagas.md): A multi-step workflow that crosses service boundaries.
- [Choreography and Orchestration](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/integration-patterns/choreography-vs-orchestration.md): Who decides the next step when a workflow is split across components.
- [Synchronous Call Chains](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/integration-patterns/synchronous-call-chains.md): A request that waits on another module, which waits on another, stacks latency and failure.

### Refactoring Patterns

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/refactoring-patterns/overview.md): Below is a bullet list of refactoring patterns from Martin Fowler's book Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code (2nd Edition). Each pattern includes its name and a brief description of its purpose.
- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/patterns/overview.md): Patterns are proven solutions to common problems. Understanding them helps you write better code and communicate with other engineers.

## SDLC

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/sdlc/overview.md): The Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) is a structured process for planning, creating, testing, deploying, and maintaining software. Below is a comprehensive list of SDLC phases, each with a brief description of its purpose and activities.
- [Architecture](https://wshaddix.com/sdlc/architecture.md): Where the code of a console app, an API, a web UI, a Windows app, and a mobile app each sits.
- [Requirements and Stories](https://wshaddix.com/sdlc/requirements-and-stories.md): How a change is described so an engineer can build it and a test can tell whether it is done.
- [Debugging](https://wshaddix.com/sdlc/debugging.md): How to find a defect: reproduce it, narrow it, fix it, and prove the fix.
- [Testing Strategy](https://wshaddix.com/sdlc/testing-strategy.md): What a unit test, an API test, a component test, and a scenario each prove. The runner for all of them on this site is TUnit.
- [Code Review](https://wshaddix.com/sdlc/code-review.md): How a change gets read before it merges.

### Version Control

- [Configuration](https://wshaddix.com/devops/version-control/git-configuration.md)

- [Branching and Pull Requests](https://wshaddix.com/devops/version-control/branching-and-pull-requests.md): How a change moves from your machine onto main.
- [Conventional Commits](https://wshaddix.com/devops/version-control/conventional-commits.md): Conventional Commits is specification for adding human and machine readable meaning to commit messages.

### CI/CD

- [Azure DevOps](https://wshaddix.com/devops/ci-cd/azure-devops.md): Microsoft's complete DevOps platform.
- [GitHub Actions](https://wshaddix.com/devops/ci-cd/github-actions.md): Automation built into GitHub for CI/CD workflows.
- [CI/CD Concepts](https://wshaddix.com/devops/ci-cd/concepts.md): Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery automate the path from code to production.

### Containerization

- [Best Practices](https://wshaddix.com/devops/containerization/best-practices.md): Building production-ready containers.
- [Docker Compose](https://wshaddix.com/devops/containerization/docker-compose.md): Define and run multi-container applications.
- [Docker Fundamentals](https://wshaddix.com/devops/containerization/docker-fundamentals.md): Containers package applications with their dependencies for consistent deployment.

### Azure

- [Blob Storage](https://wshaddix.com/devops/azure/blob-storage.md): Object storage for files the database should not hold.
- [Azure Functions](https://wshaddix.com/devops/azure/functions.md): Serverless compute for event-driven applications.
- [Azure SQL](https://wshaddix.com/devops/azure/azure-sql.md): Managed SQL Server in the cloud.
- [App Service](https://wshaddix.com/devops/azure/app-service.md): Managed platform for hosting web applications.
- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/devops/azure/overview.md): Microsoft's cloud platform with first-class .NET support.

### Monitoring

- [Alerting](https://wshaddix.com/devops/monitoring/alerting.md): Proactive notification of issues.
- [Metrics](https://wshaddix.com/devops/monitoring/metrics.md): Measuring application and infrastructure health.
- [Logging](https://wshaddix.com/devops/monitoring/logging.md): Capturing application behavior for debugging and monitoring.

### Self-Hosting

- [Self-Hosting](https://wshaddix.com/devops/self-hosting/overview.md): Run the app on a machine you control, and give the internet a way to reach it.
- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/devops/overview.md): DevOps bridges development and operations, focusing on automation, collaboration, and continuous delivery.

## Building a SaaS

### 01: Project Setup

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/building-a-saas/01-project-setup/overview.md): A well-organized project structure sets the foundation for maintainability and scalability.

### 02: Architecture

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/building-a-saas/02-architecture-decisions/overview.md): Good architecture enables teams to move fast while maintaining quality. Here we make key decisions for our SaaS platform.

### 03: Domain Modeling

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/building-a-saas/03-domain-modeling/overview.md): The domain model is the heart of your application - getting it right is crucial.

### 04: Authentication

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/building-a-saas/04-authentication/overview.md): Security is non-negotiable. We'll implement robust authentication that's also user-friendly.

### 05: Multi-Tenancy

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/building-a-saas/05-multi-tenancy/overview.md): Multi-tenancy allows one application to serve many customers with isolated data.

### 06: API Development

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/building-a-saas/06-api-development/overview.md): Well-designed APIs are a pleasure to use. We'll build RESTful endpoints that are consistent, documented, and secure.

### 07: Data Layer

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/building-a-saas/07-data-layer/overview.md): The data layer connects your domain model to the database. Done right, it's reliable and performant.

### 08: Background Jobs

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/building-a-saas/08-background-jobs/overview.md): Not everything should happen in the request/response cycle. Background jobs handle async work.

### 09: Billing

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/building-a-saas/09-billing-integration/overview.md): Monetization is what makes a SaaS sustainable. We'll integrate Stripe for subscription billing.

### 10: Testing

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/building-a-saas/10-testing-strategy/overview.md): Tests give you confidence to ship. We'll build a comprehensive testing strategy.

### 11: Deployment

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/building-a-saas/11-deployment/overview.md): Getting code to production reliably and repeatedly.

### 12: Operations

- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/building-a-saas/12-monitoring-operations/overview.md): Your job isn't done when code ships. Observability keeps your SaaS running smoothly.
- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/building-a-saas/overview.md): This is the capstone of everything documented on this site. We'll build a complete, production-ready SaaS application from scratch, applying all the concepts you've learned.

## Career Development

### Career Ladder

- [Engineering Leadership Career Path](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/career-ladder/index.md): This guide provides a comprehensive overview of the engineering leadership ladder, from Individual Contributor through VP of Engineering. Each role has its own detailed page with responsibilities, skills, and transition guidance.
- [Individual Contributor](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/career-ladder/individual-contributor.md): As an Individual Contributor (IC), you are the technical foundation of the engineering organization. Your primary focus is on craft, code quality, and technical execution.
- [Manager of Software Engineering](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/career-ladder/manager.md): As a Manager, you shift from individual technical contribution to team enablement. Your primary focus is on team execution and people development. You
- [Director of Software Engineering](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/career-ladder/director.md): As a Director, you shift from managing a single team to owning a domain across multiple teams. Your primary focus is on cross-team strategy and organizational health.
- [VP of Engineering](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/career-ladder/vp.md): As a VP, you own the entire engineering function or a major division. Your primary focus is on function-wide strategy and business outcomes. You answer the

### People Management

- [Team Building](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/people-management/team-building.md): Creating a team that's more than the sum of its parts.
- [Performance Reviews](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/people-management/performance-reviews.md): Formal evaluation of performance over a period. Should contain no surprises if 1:1s are working.
- [Hiring](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/people-management/hiring.md): Your team is only as good as the people on it. Hiring well is one of the highest-leverage activities.
- [Giving Feedback](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/people-management/feedback.md): Feedback is how people grow. Learning to give it well is a core management skill.
- [One-on-Ones](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/people-management/one-on-ones.md): The 1:1 is the most important meeting you have as a manager. It's dedicated time for your direct report.

### Team Operations

- [Capacity Planning](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/team-operations/capacity-planning.md): Understanding and allocating team capacity for sustainable delivery.
- [Training Curation](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/team-operations/training-curation.md): Curating learning resources to help your team grow.
- [Skill Matrices](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/team-operations/skill-matrices.md): A skill matrix maps team capabilities to identify gaps and plan development.

### Soft Skills

- [Stakeholder Management](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/soft-skills/stakeholder-management.md): Working effectively with people outside your team who have interest in your work.
- [Presentations](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/soft-skills/presentations.md): Presenting effectively amplifies your influence and helps you advance.
- [Technical Writing](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/soft-skills/technical-writing.md): Clear writing is clear thinking. Technical writing skills help you communicate effectively.
- [Overview](https://wshaddix.com/career-development/overview.md): Technical skills get you hired. Career skills help you grow, lead, and make an impact.
